question: According to Politico, the EU has issued a call for tenders to enable its senior officials to travel more frequently on business by air taxi. In fact, the EU plans to spend up to EUR 16 million over the next four years to fly its senior officials by private jet1.

It is worth noting that a previous contract (2016-2021) had been signed to the tune of EUR 7 million, which was then increased to EUR 11 million when the ‘green’ Von der Leyen Commission took office2.

At the same time, some European citizens and consumers are, or will be, faced with a ban on using their cars because they emit too much CO2, even if they are elderly or would prefer to spend their money on something other than a new car. 1.
In 2025, what flights did the Commission and other institutions take, respectively?

Why does the Commission still not make public the purpose of these trips, especially when a flight to Central Asia in 2024, costing EUR 100 000, and taken by a commissioner responsible for ‘promoting the European way of life’, Margarítis Schinás, might come as a surprise to some?

Given that the contract concerns the transport of protected Eurocrats, what does the following clause in the call for tenders mean: ‘Terms of contract: The execution of the contract must be performed within the framework of sheltered employment programmes: No’?
answer: on behalf of the European Commission (15.6.2026) 1. In 2025, 27 air-chartered services were used by the President of the Commission or other Commissioners. Information on missions of Members of the Commission is available on the European Commission website1. The Commission does not provide information on behalf of other institutions. 2.

The Commission publishes an overview of mission expenses and purpose per Member every two months in accordance with the Code of Conduct2. Information on missions of former Vice-President of the European Commission, Commissioner responsible for ‘Promoting our European Way of Life’ is publicly available3. 3.

The clause ‘Terms of contract: The execution of the contract must be performed within the framework of sheltered employment programmes: No’ means that the contractor is not required to apply a specific type of work arrangement designed to fit the needs of persons with disabilities and to have a minimum number of employees with disabilities.

However, according to the tender specifications, the contractor shall establish, maintain and promote an open and inclusive working environment, notably through the removal of all obstacles to recruitment and all potential discrimination based on disability.
